Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):
  • Acute gastroenteritis – 3-day history of profuse watery diarrhea (hourly while awake), midline intermittent crampy abdominal pain (~6/10), occasional nausea/vomiting (triggered by milk), subjective fever, decreased urine frequency.  
  • Social smoking and episodic binge alcohol use (lifestyle risk factors for chronic disease).

- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):
  • Father: Stage 3 colon cancer (details limited).  
  • Brother: Similar recent diarrheal illness (infective contact).

- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:
  • Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
  • No regular prescription medications.  
  • No known drug allergies.

- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):
  • Not recorded.

- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks:
  • Not recorded.

- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use:
  • Physical activity and general diet not discussed; patient often buys takeaway.  
  • Tobacco: Social smoker (mainly on Fridays).  
  • Alcohol: Occasional beer during weekdays; binge drinking once or twice per month; advised to avoid alcohol while unwell.  
  • No other substance use documented.

- Hearing and vision concerns:
  • Not recorded.

- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm):
  • Not recorded.

- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors:
  • Lives with mother and sister; brother lives elsewhere.  
  • Works in a government office; reluctant to take sick leave, creating work-related stress.  
  • Does not usually share meals with family; manages health issues independently.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification
  • Discussed importance of hydration; advised oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte) and clear fluids.  
  • Recommended soft diet (soups, mashed foods) progressing as tolerated.  
  • Advised to avoid alcohol until recovered.  
  • Encouraged monitoring of urine output and fever.
